title: Blossom end rot in tomato - Kenya

Header: Blossom end rot in tomato - Kenya

Prevention: Test your soil for calcium levels 1-2 months before planting and apply calcium-containing products if required.
Boost calcium levels in the soil by adding materials like very finely crushed egg shells, and bone meal in the planting hole.
Apply sufficient water regularly to keep the soil moist throughout the cropping period but do not overwater.
Mulch using materials e.g. maize stover, wheat straw or dried grass to conserve soil moisture, especially during the flowering and fruiting stage.
Harden seedlings for 2 weeks before transplanting to enhance plant vigour.
Monitoring: Small water-soaked sunken spots at the blossom ends of immature fruits which enlarge and darken as the fruits mature.
Direct Control: Blossom end rot is a physiological disorder caused by calcium deficiency.
It does not spread as diseases do.
Regularly water the crop to ensure adequate moisture for steady growth.
Enrich the soil with organic matter or use mulch to retain moisture, especially during the flowering and fruiting stage.
Restrictions: Apply soil amendments at an appropriate rate (depending on soil test results).
When applying fertilizers always wear protective equipment.
Top-dress with calcium ammonium nitrate (26%N), if the
N levels are low at knee height at an appropriate rate (depending on soil/ plant analysis results).
Ensure adequate soil moisture during application.
Follow instructions on the label such as dosage, timing of application and maximum number of applications.
Make sure the soil nitrogen levels don't become excessive.
Spray with calcium nitrate or calcium chloride at an appropriate rate (depending on soil/ plant analysis results).
Dispose of excess fertilizer properly to avoid environmental contamination.
Always use recommended fertilizer types and rates.
